dedupe_keys.name: new residential construction and survey of construction housing starts completions and characteristics

description: New Residential Construction is the U.S. Census Bureau's monthly release of national and regional counts of new privately owned housing units authorised by building permits, authorised but not started, started, under construction and completed. Permit data come from the Building Permits Survey and start and completion data from the Survey of Construction (SOC), which is partly funded by the Department of Housing and Urban Development; the SOC also publishes sales of new single-family houses and the characteristics of new single-family and multifamily housing completed, such as floor area, heating system and fuel, air conditioning, foundation and number of storeys. Coverage: the United States and its four census regions; monthly, with quarterly starts and completions by purpose and design and annual characteristics tables. Access: release tables and historical time series in XLSX, the characteristics tables and public use microdata of the SOC, and the Census Data API economic indicators time series; free and public domain. Caveats: national and regional only (local permit counts are in the Building Permits Survey), HUD-code manufactured homes are excluded, and imputation methods changed in February 2025. Simulation uses: tracking additions to the housing stock and the characteristics of new buildings, for example heating fuel and cooling, in building energy and exposure models and in scenarios of demand growth. Related records: the Building Permits Survey (the permit component), Construction Spending, Population and Housing Unit Estimates and the American Housing Survey.
